headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can leak business data, while the zoomcamp can amplify unsafe assumptions if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not a default pathway. However, agent_a has broad network egress and agent_b is a course/workflow artifact with no isolation details; if outputs are manually copied or shared through files, injected content could be misread. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not evidenced.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a outputs into agent_b-managed files or prompts
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw outputs into downstream prompts
Add a short human review step before reusing any generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches business data and has broad network egress, while agent_b has no declared data classes or egress. In a shared workspace or manual handoff, business data from agent_a could be exposed beyond the intended boundary. The interaction is plausible in default operational use, but the evidence is indirect.
conditions: IF agent_a processes business data in the same workspace used to transfer artifacts to agent_b
IF agent_b is given files containing business data from agent_a
mitigations: Separate input/output directories per agent
Redact business data before handoff
Restrict agent_a egress to approved destinations
Audit transferred files for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can egress broadly, but agent_b has no write, network, or OAuth scopes documented, so direct resource contention is not shown. The main conflict risk is operational rather than technical: if both are pointed at the same mutable dataset or workspace, agent_a’s integration behavior could interfere with agent_b’s course artifacts. Uncertainty keeps this at low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same shared dataset or directory
IF agent_b is extended with write or network permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate datasets to each agent
Freeze shared artifacts before downstream use
Review any permission changes before enabling them
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can produce data outputs that may be treated as authoritative, and agent_b is a data-engineering course artifact that could be used to operationalize those outputs. Because no verification or orchestration safeguards are documented, a bad transformation or mistaken assumption from agent_a could cascade into downstream work products. The pathway is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-produced artifacts without validation
IF downstream users treat transformed outputs as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on transferred data
Have a human compare samples before reuse
Label agent_a outputs as untrusted until verified
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation tests

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches business data and has broad egress, but no residency, retention, or regulated-data claims are documented for either agent. agent_b has no declared data classes or compliance surfaces, so a specific compliance breach is not evidenced. The risk is limited to generic policy mismatch if business data is moved across environments.
conditions: IF business data subject to internal retention rules is exported through agent_a
IF agent_b is used in an environment with stricter residency or logging rules than agent_a
mitigations: Confirm data-handling policy before transfer
Avoid sending regulated data through either agent
Document retention expectations for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: align logging and retention controls
